Convert a Stan program to the ilike language

Source: R/convert_stan.R
convert_stan_model.Rd

Translates a Stan program into a model in the ilike language, with a data section holding the data given, so that it can be run by any of ilike's algorithms. What is translated: the blocks data, transformed data, parameters, transformed parameters and model (generated quantities are left out, with a warning; functions blocks are refused); declarations of int, real, vector, row_vector, matrix, simplex, cov_matrix and corr_matrix variables, arrays of them (array[N] real and the older real y[N]), with lower and upper bounds; for loops; assignments (as deterministic nodes); sampling statements, vectorised ones included (as loops over the elements), with truncation T[a, b] for normal; target += with a log density function (y ~ dist(...) written as target += dist_lpdf(y | ...)) or an expression; arithmetic, element-wise functions (exp, log, sqrt, square, inv_logit, logit, inv, fabs, abs, log1p, expm1, lgamma, sin, cos, tanh, fmin, fmax, pow), and matrix-vector products X * beta whose inner length is known from the data. Distributions: normal, std_normal, lognormal, gamma, inv_gamma, beta, exponential, uniform, cauchy, student_t, double_exponential, logistic, weibull, chi_square, von_mises, poisson, poisson_log, bernoulli, bernoulli_logit, binomial, binomial_logit, neg_binomial, neg_binomial_2, categorical, multinomial, dirichlet, multi_normal, multi_student_t, wishart, inv_wishart, lkj_corr. A constrained parameter's prior becomes the distribution on its support (normal with bounds: tnorm; normal(0, s), cauchy(0, s) and student_t(nu, 0, s) with lower = 0: halfnorm, halfcauchy, halft); a parameter with both bounds and no prior gets the uniform distribution, a simplex the uniform Dirichlet and a correlation matrix lkj(1). Anything else (if, while, user-defined functions, improper priors, other constraints) stops with a message naming the statement.

The ilike model has proper priors and normalised densities, so its evidence is that of the model; Stan's target drops constants, which does not change the posterior. An algorithm section is added with a NUTS move on all the parameters (with dual averaging of the step over the first 1000 iterations), when they can all be moved by it.

Usage

convert_stan_model(model, data = list(), output = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

model

The Stan program: a file name, or the program as a character string.

data

A list with the data, named as in the data block.

output

(optional) The file to write.

overwrite

(optional) If TRUE, an existing output file is replaced.

Value

Invisibly, the converted text.
